title: Morse-Smale parallel decomposer + live overlay (Phase B)
description:
PATCH-22 Phase A shipped a Morse-Smale diagnostic on the skull and validated the approach. PATCH-23 builds a parallel decomposer (MorseSmaleDecomposer) alongside SemanticPatchDecomposer, with a runtime selector. Both pipelines coexist; we A/B compare on the skull and other meshes.

Phase B has 4 sub-stages, each visually verified:

B1. Proper PL-Morse classifier (ordered 1-ring + lower-link components → correct multi-saddle handling) + filtered union-find persistence pairing + cancellation. Replaces Phase A's prominence approximation and 2-ring NMS.

B2. Closed-cell assembly: walk arc graph CCW around each max → 2-cells. Output looks like the kitten reference.

B3. Feature-edge snapping (Dong 2005 §4): banded shortest-path that pulls MSC arcs onto crest/saddle/multi-source feature edges. Combines MSC topology with our existing curated feature-edge set.

B4. Coons-error refinement (handles cranium-style smooth regions) + integration as MorseSmaleDecomposer producing the same DecompositionDiagnostics record. Live viewer gets a `D` key to cycle SEMANTIC ↔ MORSE_SMALE decomposers.

Live-viewer ShaderMode.MSC mode also added (user's explicit ask) — routes through PATCH-17 depth-aware overlay infrastructure.

Plan file: ~/.claude/plans/plan-written-targets-crest-line-swirling-garden.md (reused per session). Research basis: Robins-Wood-Sheppard discrete gradient, Edelsbrunner persistence, Dong 2005 spectral quadrangulation arc-snapping, Bommes 2009 MIQ for cell refinement.
definition-of-done:
1. New MorseSmaleDecomposer.java produces a working PatchDecomposition compatible with all existing rendering / Coons-error / automation infrastructure.
2. Decomposer selector (`D` key) cycles between SEMANTIC and MORSE_SMALE in the live viewer; cachedDiagnostics invalidates and rebuilds on switch.
3. ShaderMode.MSC overlay in the live viewer renders critical points (red/blue/yellow dots) and integral arcs (black lines) with PATCH-17 depth occlusion.
4. On skull: MSC cells visually match the kitten reference (closed quad-like cells, each with one extremum). Cranium splits into multiple cells via Coons-error refinement.
5. Coons p95 from MorseSmaleDecomposer is comparable to or better than SemanticPatchDecomposer on the skull.
6. SemanticPatchDecomposer pipeline is untouched (no regressions to PATCH-14..21 work).
testing-plan:
Each sub-stage is its own checkpoint:

B1: rerun MSC overlay on skull, expect 100% arc-connection rate vs Phase A's 72%, fewer face-region false positives.
B2: overlay shows closed cells; visually compare to kitten reference.
B3: STAGES + MSC side-by-side composite shows cell boundaries snap onto feature edges.
B4: VerifyCoonsError runner on the new decomposer; live viewer cycles between decomposers via `D`; flat-patch render compares directly.
